###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 35

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/35](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/35)


**מוֹדִים** אֲנַֽחְנוּ לָךְ שָׁאַתָּה הוּא יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד צוּר חַיֵּֽינוּ מָגֵן יִשְׁעֵֽנוּ אַתָּה הוּא לְדוֹר וָדוֹר נוֹדֶה לְּךָ וּנְסַפֵּר תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ עַל חַיֵּֽינוּ הַמְּסוּרִים בְּיָדֶֽךָ וְעַל נִשְׁמוֹתֵֽינוּ הַפְּקוּדוֹת לָךְ וְעַל נִסֶּֽיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם עִמָּֽנוּ וְעַל נִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ וְטוֹבוֹתֶֽיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל עֵת, עֶֽרֶב וָבֹֽקֶר וְצָהֳרָֽיִם, הַטּוֹב כִּי לֹא כָלוּ רַחֲמֶֽיךָ וְהַמְרַחֵם כִּי לֹא תַֽמּוּ חֲסָדֶֽיךָ, מֵעוֹלָם קִוִּֽינוּ לָךְ:


**We** are thankful to You that You Adonoy are our God and the God of our fathers forever; Rock of our lives, Shield of our deliverance, You are in every generation. We will give thanks to You and recount Your praise, for our lives which are committed into Your hand, and for our souls which are entrusted to You, and for Your miracles of every day with us, and for Your wonders and benefactions at all times— evening, morning and noon. (You are) The Beneficent One— for Your compassion is never withheld; And (You are) the Merciful One— for Your kindliness never ceases; we have always placed our hope in You.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 36

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/36](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/36)


**וְעַל** כֻּלָּם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִתְרוֹמַם שִׁמְךָ מַלְכֵּֽנוּ תָּמִיד לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד: וּכְתוֹב לְחַיִּים טוֹבִים כָּל בְּנֵי בְרִיתֶֽךָ:


**And** for all the foregoing blessed and exalted be your Name, our King constantly, forever and ever. Inscribe for a good life all the children of Your covenant.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 38

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/38](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/38)


וְכֹל הַחַיִּים יוֹדֽוּךָ סֶּֽלָה וִיהַלְלוּ אֶת שִׁמְךָ בֶּאֱמֶת הָאֵל יְשׁוּעָתֵֽנוּ וְעֶזְרָתֵֽנוּ סֶֽלָה: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה הַטּוֹב שִׁמְךָ וּלְךָ נָאֶה לְהוֹדוֹת:


And all the living shall thank You forever and praise Your Name with sincerity the Almighty, Who is our deliverance and our help forever. Blessed are You, Adonoy, “The Beneficent” is Your Name and You it is fitting to praise.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 39

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/39](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/39)


**שלום**


**PRAYER FOR PEACE**


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 40

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/40](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/40)


**שִׂים**שָׁלוֹם טוֹבָה וּבְרָכָה חֵן וָחֶֽסֶד וְרַחֲמִים עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּֽךָ, בָּרְכֵֽנוּ אָבִֽינוּ כֻּלָּֽנוּ כְּאֶחָד בְּאוֹר פָּנֶֽיךָ כִּי בְאוֹר פָּנֶֽיךָ נָתַֽתָּ לָּֽנוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ תּוֹרַת חַיִּים וְאַהֲבַת חֶֽסֶד וּצְדָקָה וּבְרָכָה וְרַחֲמִים וְחַיִּים וְשָׁלוֹם, וְטוֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל עֵת וּבְכָל שָׁעָה בִּשְׁלוֹמֶֽךָ: בְּסֵֽפֶר חַיִּים בְּרָכָה וְשָׁלוֹם וּפַרְנָסָה טוֹבָה נִזָּכֵר וְנִכָּתֵב לְפָנֶֽיךָ אֲנַֽחְנוּ וְכָל עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל לְחַיִּים טוֹבִים וּלְשָׁלוֹם: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה עֹשֶׂה הַשָּׁלוֹם: הַמְּבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּשָּׁלוֹם:


Grant peace, goodness, and blessing, favor, kindness and compassion upon us and upon all Yisrael, Your people. Bless us, our Father, all of us as one with the light of Your countenance. For by the light of Your countenance You gave us Adonoy our God, a Torah of life and the love of kindliness, righteousness, blessing, compassion, life, and peace. And may it be good in Your eyes and to bless Your people Yisrael, at all times and at every moment with Your peace. In the book of life, blessing, peace and abundant maintenance, may we be remembered and inscribed before You; we and all Your people, the House of Yisrael for a good life and peace. 
*If you forgot to say this, you need not go back and repeat the Amidah.*
 Blessed are You, Adonoy, Who makes the peace. 
*(others conclude—*
 Who blesses His people Yisrael with peace.)


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 41

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/41](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/41)


יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה צוּרִי וְגוֹאֲלִי:


May the words of my mouth be acceptable and the thoughts of my heart — before You Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 42

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/42](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/42)


אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ תָּבֹא לְפָנֶֽיךָ תְּפִלָּתֵֽנוּ, וְאַל תִּתְעַלַּם מִתְּחִנָּתֵֽנוּ שֶׁאֵין אֲנַֽחְנוּ עַזֵּי פָנִים וּקְשֵׁי עֹֽרֶף לוֹמַר לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ צַדִּיקִים אֲנַֽחְנוּ וְלֹא חָטָֽאנוּ אֲבָל אֲנַֽחְנוּ וַאֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ חָטָֽאנוּ:


Our God and God of our fathers, let our prayer come before you and do not ignore our supplication. For we are not so brazen-faced and stiff-necked to say to you, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, “We are righteous and have not sinned.” But, indeed, we and our fathers have sinned.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 43

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/43](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/43)


אָשַֽׁמְנוּ. בָּגַֽדְנוּ. גָּזַֽלְנוּ. דִּבַּֽרְנוּ דֹּֽפִי. הֶעֱוִֽינוּ. וְהִרְשַֽׁעְנוּ. זַֽדְנוּ. חָמַֽסְנוּ. טָפַֽלְנוּ שֶֽׁקֶר. יָעַֽצְנוּ רָע. כִּזַּֽבְנוּ. לַֽצְנוּ. מָרַֽדְנוּ. נִאַֽצְנוּ. סָרַֽרְנוּ. עָוִֽינוּ. פָּשַֽׁעְנוּ. צָרַֽרְנוּ. קִשִּֽׁינוּ עֹֽרֶף. רָשַֽׁעְנוּ. שִׁחַֽתְנוּ. תִּעַֽבְנוּ. תָּעִֽינוּ. תִּעְתָּֽעְנוּ:


We have trespassed [against God and man, and we are devastated by our guilt]; We have betrayed [God and man, we have been ungrateful for the good done to us]; We have stolen; We have slandered. We have caused others to sin; We have caused others to commit sins for which they are called רְשָׁעִים, wicked; We have sinned with malicious intent; We have forcibly taken others' possessions even though we paid for them; We have added falsehood upon falsehood; We have joined with evil individuals or groups; We have given harmful advice; We have deceived; we have mocked; We have rebelled against God and His Torah; We have caused God to be angry with us; We have turned away from God's Torah; We have sinned deliberately; We have been negligent in our performance of the commandments; We have caused our friends grief; We have been stiff-necked, refusing to admit that our suffering is caused by our own sins. We have committed sins for which we are called רָשָׁע, [raising a hand to hit someone]. We have committed sins which are the result of moral corruption; We have committed sins which the Torah refers to as abominations; We have gone astray; We have led others astray.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 44

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/44](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/44)


סַֽרְנוּ מִמִּצְוֹתֶֽיךָ וּמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ הַטּוֹבִים וְלֹא שָֽׁוָה לָֽנוּ. וְאַתָּה צַדִּיק עַל כָּל הַבָּא עָלֵֽינוּ. כִּי אֱמֶת עָשִֽׂיתָ וַאֲנַֽחְנוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ:


We have turned away from Your commandments and from Your good laws, and we have gained nothing from it. And You are the Righteous One in all [punishment] that has come upon us; for You have acted truthfully and we have acted wickedly.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 45

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/45](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/45)


מַה נֹּאמַר לְפָנֶֽיךָ יוֹשֵׁב מָרוֹם. וּמַה נְּסַפֵּר לְפָנֶֽיךָ שׁוֹכֵן שְׁחָקִים. הֲלֹא כָּל הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת וְהַנִּגְלוֹת אַתָּה יוֹדֵֽעַ:


What shall we say before You, Who dwells on high; and what shall we relate to You Who dwells in the heavens? For everything, both hidden and revealed, You know.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 46

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/46](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/46)


אַתָּה יוֹדֵֽעַ רָזֵי עוֹלָם. וְתַעֲלוּמוֹת סִתְרֵי כָל חָי: אַתָּה חוֹפֵשׂ כָּל חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן וּבוֹחֵן כְּלָיוֹת וָלֵב: אֵין דָּבָר נֶעְלָם מִמֶּֽךָּ. וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מִנֶּֽגֶד עֵינֶֽיךָ:


You know the mysteries of the universe, and the hidden secrets of every individual. You search all our innermost thoughts, and probe our mind and heart. There is nothing hidden from You, and there is nothing concealed from Your sight.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 47

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/47](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/47)


וּבְכֵן יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ. שֶׁתְּכַפֵּר לָֽנוּ עַל כָּל חַטֹּאתֵֽינוּ. וְתִסְלַח לָֽנוּ עַל כָּל עֲו‍ֹנוֹתֵֽינוּ. וּתִמְחָל לָֽנוּ עַל כָּל פְּשָׁעֵֽינוּ:


And so may it be Your will Adonoy our God and God of our fathers, that You pardon us for all our careless sins, and that You forgive us for all our deliberate sins, and that You grant us atonement for all our rebellious sins:


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 48

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/48](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/48)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּאֹֽנֶס וּבְרָצוֹן:


For the sin we committed before You under compulsion³⁹ and willingly.

footnotes:
³⁹ Even a sin committed under duress needs to be forgiven, because many times a person allows himself to be placed in a predicament in which he is compelled to sin (e.g., leaving the office at a very late hour on the eve of Shabbos or Festival).—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 49

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/49](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/49)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּאִמּוּץ הַלֵּב:


And for the sin we committed before You by callously hardening the heart.⁴⁰

footnotes:
⁴⁰ This would include not giving charity with a whole heart, and not helping a needy fellow Jew.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 50

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/50](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/50)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּבְלִי דָֽעַת:


For the sin we committed before You inadvertently.⁴¹

footnotes:
⁴¹ The literal meaning of בִּבְלִי דַעַת is “without knowledge,” and it implies not using our intellectual capabilities to study the laws of Torah and therewith gain the “knowledge” needed to observe the commandments properly.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 51

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/51](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/51)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּבִטּוּי שְׂפָתָֽיִם:


And for the sin we committed before You with an utterance of the lips.⁴²

footnotes:
⁴² This includes the sins of making vows and oaths (even though they are kept), verbally insulting one’s fellowmen, and directing one’s displeasure against the decrees of Hashem.— Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 52

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/52](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/52)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּגָלוּי וּבַסָּֽתֶר:


For the sin we committed before You openly and secretly.⁴³

footnotes:
⁴³ A sin committed publicly could very well cause חִלוּל ה', the desecration of Hashem’s Name, and may also lead others to sin. A sin committed in secret, indicates that the sinner fears the reaction of people but is unafraid of Hashem’s displeasure.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 53

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/53](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/53)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּגִלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת:


And for the sin we committed before You in sexual immorality.⁴⁴

footnotes:
⁴⁴ This also includes such things that arouse desire for forbidden sexual relationships, such as embracing or dancing.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 54

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/54](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/54)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּדִבּוּר פֶּה:


For the sin we committed before You through [misuse of our power of] speech.⁴⁵

footnotes:
⁴⁵ This includes speaking the words of Torah in unclean places, cursing, humiliating someone; speaking of business matters on Shabbos, revealing another person’s secret, telling jokes and holding idle conversations in a house of worship (and certainly during the actual prayers) and telling lies.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 55

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/55](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/55)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּדַעַת וּבְמִרְמָה:


And for the sin we committed before You with knowledge and with deceit.⁴⁶

footnotes:
⁴⁶ This includes false advertising and dishonesty in business matters.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 56

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/56](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/56)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּהַרְהוֹר הַלֵּב:


For the sin we committed before You by improper thoughts.⁴⁷

footnotes:
⁴⁷ Evil thoughts, lustful thoughts, heretical thoughts, and suspicious thoughts about righteous people are included.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 57

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/57](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/57)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּהוֹנָֽאַת רֵֽעַ:


And for the sin we committed before You by cheating a fellow-man.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 58

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/58](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/58)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּוִדּוּי פֶּה:


For the sin we committed before You with [mere] verbal confession.⁴⁸

footnotes:
⁴⁸ This refers to confession of sins without feeling regret for committing them and without earnest resolve to correct them in the future.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 59

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/59](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/59)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּוְעִידַת זְנוּת:


And for the sin we committed before You by joining in a lewd gathering.⁴⁹

footnotes:
⁴⁹ Any gathering or intimate meeting for the purpose of sexual immortality is included.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 60

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/60](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/60)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּזָדוֹן וּבִשְׁגָגָה:


For the sin we committed before You intentionally and unintentionally.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 61

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/61](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/61)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּזִלְזוּל הוֹרִים וּמוֹרִים:


And for the sin we committed before You by insufficient respect for parents and teachers.⁵⁰

footnotes:
⁵⁰ Not obeying their commands, not rising for a talmudic scholar and disrespect for one’s teacher even if he is not considered a “Torah Great” are included.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 62

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/62](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/62)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּחֹֽזֶק יָד:


For the sin we committed before You by using coercion [to harm others].⁵¹

footnotes:
⁵¹ This includes using physical, political or financial power to harm someone.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 63

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/63](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/63)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּחִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם:


And for the sin we committed before You by desecrating the Divine Name.⁵²

footnotes:
⁵² This involves any sin committed that becomes public knowledge, including improper conduct with one’s fellow man.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 64

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/64](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/64)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּטִפְשׁוּת פֶּה:


For the sin we committed before You with foolish talk.⁵³

footnotes:
⁵³ This refers to idle talk and gossip.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 65

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/65](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/65)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּטֻמְאַת שְׂפָתָֽיִם:


And for the sin we committed before You with impurity of the lips.⁵⁴

footnotes:
⁵⁴ This includes profanity and unclean language.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 66

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/66](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/66)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּיֵֽצֶר הָרָע:


For the sin we committed before You with the Evil Inclination.⁵⁵

footnotes:
⁵⁵ When a person allows his Evil Inclination to rule over him, he commits a sin.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 67

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/67](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/67)

And for the sin we committed before You knowingly and unknowingly.⁵⁶

footnotes:
⁵⁶ We ask Hashem to pardon us even for sins we are not aware that we committed, and also for such sins through which we caused damage but are not aware of the amount of loss incurred. —Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 68

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/68](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/68)

And for all of these, God of pardon, pardon us, forgive us, grant us atonement.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 69

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/69](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/69)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּכַפַּת שֹֽׁחַד:


For the sin we committed before You by forcing someone to give or take bribes.⁵⁷

footnotes:
⁵⁷ A bribe is not limited to money or gifts; it includes flattery or personal favors.— Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 70

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/70](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/70)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּכַֽחַשׁ וּבְכָזָב:


And for the sin we committed before You by false denial and false promise.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 71

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/71](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/71)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע:


For the sin we committed before You by evil talk [slander].⁵⁸

footnotes:
⁵⁸ This includes causing a fellow Jew physical, monetary of social harm through passing degrading information about him to another person. It makes no difference whether this is done in his presence or behind his back, or if the information is true or false.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 72

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/72](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/72)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּלָצוֹן:


And for the sin we committed before You by scoffing.⁵⁹

footnotes:
⁵⁹ Ridicule of a person, a commandment, or guards of Torah are all included in the sin of scoffing.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 73

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/73](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/73)

For the sin we committed before You in business dealings.⁶⁰

footnotes:
⁶⁰ This would include overcharging, misrepresenting, false-labeling and all other such deceitful practices.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 74

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/74](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/74)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּמַאֲכָל וּבְמִשְׁתֶּה:


And for the sin we committed before You in eating and drinking.⁶¹

footnotes:
⁶¹ Eating forbidden (non-kosher) foods, not saying the proper blessing or grace after meals, over-eating, are included in this sin.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 75

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/75](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/75)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּנֶֽשֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּית:


For the sin we committed before You by [taking or giving] interest and by usury.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 76

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/76](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/76)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּנְטִיַּת גָּרוֹן:


And for the sin we committed before You by haughtily stretching forth the neck.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 77

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/77](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/77)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּשִׂקּוּר עָֽיִן:


For the sin we committed before You with gazing of the eyes.⁶²

footnotes:
⁶² This refers to using the eyes to gaze at forbidden things.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 78

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/78](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/78)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּשִֽׂיחַ שִׂפְתוֹתֵֽינוּ:


And for the sin we committed before You by the prattle of our lips.⁶³

footnotes:
⁶³ This includes idle gossip, which is certainly forbidden in the synagogue at all times.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 79

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/79](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/79)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּעֵינַֽיִם רָמוֹת:


For the sin we committed before You with haughty eyes.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 80

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/80](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/80)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּעַזּוּת מֶֽצַח:


And for the sin we committed before You with impudence.⁶⁴

footnotes:
⁶⁴ Speaking “with chutzpah” to Torah scholars, or to someone more learned than himself is included in עַזּוּת מֵצַח.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 81

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/81](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/81)


וְעַל כֻּלָּם אֱלֽוֹהַּ סְלִיחוֹת. סְלַח לָֽנוּ. מְחַל לָֽנוּ. כַּפֶּר לָֽנוּ:


And for all of these, God of pardon, pardon us, forgive us, grant us atonement.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 82

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/82](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/82)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּפְרִֽיקַת עֹל:


For the sin we committed before You by throwing off the yoke [of heaven].⁶⁵

footnotes:
⁶⁵ Rejecting an obligation to fulfill even a single commandment. Also included is shirking a religious obligation which must then be assumed by someone else.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 83

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/83](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/83)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּפְלִילוּת:


And for the sin we committed before You in passing judgment.⁶⁶

footnotes:
⁶⁶ This includes a “Dayan,” a judge who does not render correct decisions, and it also includes not giving someone the benefit of the doubt.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 84

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/84](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/84)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּצְדִיַּת רֵֽעַ:


For the sin we committed before You by entrapping a fellowman.⁶⁷

footnotes:
⁶⁷ This includes even attempting to harm someone; even if no harm was actually done, he still needs forgiveness.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 85

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/85](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/85)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּצָרוּת עָֽיִן:


And for the sin we committed before You by a begrudging eye.⁶⁸

footnotes:
⁶⁸ Not doing a favor, not giving charity properly, and feeling bad at someone else’s success are included.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 86

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/86](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/86)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ:


For the sin we committed before You by lightmindedness.⁶⁹

footnotes:
⁶⁹ Lightmindedness or frivolity in the synagogue or Bais Midrash or while wearing tefillin are serious sins.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 87

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/87](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/87)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּקַשְׁיוּת עֹֽרֶף:


And for the sin we committed before You by being stiff-necked [stubborn].⁷⁰

footnotes:
⁷⁰ Rejecting admonition and “ignoring” punishment are included. Also included is brushing aside illness, financial loss, and humiliation as mere coincidences rather than manifestations of Divine displeasure.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 88

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/88](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/88)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּרִיצַת רַגְלַֽיִם לְהָרַע:


For the sin we committed before You by running to do evil.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 89

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/89](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/89)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּרְכִילוּת:


And for the sin we committed before You by talebearing.⁷¹

footnotes:
⁷¹ This refers to carrying tales, even true ones, about one person to another, and the one who listens to these tales is also included in this category of sin.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 90

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/90](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/90)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּשְׁבֽוּעַת שָׁוְא:


For the sin we committed before You by swearing in vain.⁷²

footnotes:
⁷² This includes swearing falsely or even swearing a useless oath.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 91

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/91](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/91)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּשִׂנְאַת חִנָּם:


And for the sin we committed before You by unwarranted hatred.⁷³

footnotes:
⁷³ Hating someone because of jealousy, or because he doesn’t conform to your ideas of ettiquete.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 92

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/92](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/92)


עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בִּתְשֽׂוּמֶת יָד:


For the sin we committed before You by breach of trust.⁷⁴

footnotes:
⁷⁴ Denying that you owe someone a monetary debt when he asks for payment.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 93

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/93](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/93)


וְעַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָֽאנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ בְּתִמְהוֹן לֵבָב:


And for the sin we committed before You by a confused heart.⁷⁵

footnotes:
⁷⁵ This includes sins committed because of confusion, worry or pain, it also includes the sin of harboring doubts about the authenticity of the laws enacted by our Sages, and doubts about the fundamental principles of our faith, such as Divine Providence, reward and punishment, and also doubts about the authenticity of the Torah and the Prophets.—Siddur HaGra


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 94

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/94](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/94)


וְעַל כֻּלָּם אֱלֽוֹהַּ סְלִיחוֹת. סְלַח לָֽנוּ. מְחַל לָֽנוּ. כַּפֶּר לָֽנוּ:


And for all of these, God of pardon, pardon us, forgive us, grant us atonement.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 95

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/95](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/95)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹלָה:


And for sins for which we are obligated to bring a burnt-offering.⁷⁶

footnotes:
⁷⁶ A burnt-offering is brought for failure to fulfill any positive commandment, e.g, putting on non-kosher tefillin.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 96

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/96](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/96)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם חַטָּאת:


And for sins for which we are obligated to bring a sin-offering.⁷⁷

footnotes:
⁷⁷ A sin-offering is brought for unintentionally transgressing any prohibitive commandment punishable by excision (כָּרֵת) if it were done with intent.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 97

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/97](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/97)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם קָרְבַּן עוֹלֶה וְיוֹרֵד:


And for sins for which we are obligated to bring a “fluctuating” offering.⁷⁸

footnotes:
⁷⁸ The fluctuating offering is an offering that varies in value according to the financial means of the individual who brings it. (The literal meaning of עוֹלָה וְיוֹרֵד, is “go up and down”). This type of offering is brought when a person swore falsely (unintentionally) concerning something he did or did not do. For example, one may have thought he ate something and consequently swore that he ate it, but in reality he did not and thus he swore falsely.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 98

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/98](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/98)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם אָשָׁם וַדַּאי וְתָלוּי:


And for sins for which we are obligated to bring a guilt-offering for certain or for doubtful trespasses.⁷⁹

footnotes:
⁷⁹ This type of sacrifice was brought in an instance where it is uncertain whether or not a violation occurred. For example it is not known whether a substance he ate was of a forbidden nature or if it was permitted.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 99

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/99](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/99)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם מַכַּת מַרְדּוּת:


And for sins for which we incur the penalty of lashing for violations of Rabbinic law.⁸⁰

footnotes:
⁸⁰ A Rabbinic Court had the right to impose lashing for a violation of a rabbinic injunction.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 100

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/100](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/100)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם מַלְקוּת אַרְבָּעִים:


And for sins for which we incur the penalty of forty lashes.⁸¹

footnotes:
⁸¹ Forty lashes proscribed by the Torah was given to one who actively and intentionally violated any of the prohibitive commandments, providing he was forewarned and the act was witnessed by two witnesses.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 101

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/101](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/101)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה בִּידֵי שָׁמָֽיִם:


And for sins for which we incur the penalty of death at the hand of Heaven.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 102

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/102](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/102)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם כָּרֵת וַעֲרִירִי:


And for sins for which we incur the penalty of excision and childlessness.⁸²

footnotes:
⁸² One who intentionally does work or eats on Yom Kippur, or one who eats chometz — leavened bread — on Pesach, is punished with excision and childlessness.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 103

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/103](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/103)


וְעַל חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָֽנוּ חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין. סְקִילָה. שְׂרֵפָה. הֶֽרֶג. וְחֶֽנֶק.


And for sins for which we are liable to any of the four death penalties inflicted by the [Rabbinic] Court [which are]: stoning, burning, beheading or strangulation.⁸³

footnotes:
⁸³ Stoning is the penalty for knowingly desecrating Shabbos, burning is the penalty for certain forbidden sexual relationships, beheading is the penalty for murder, and strangulation is the penalty for adultery.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 104

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/104](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/104)


עַל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה וְעַל מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה. בֵּין שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ קוּם עֲשֵׂה. וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ קוּם עֲשֵׂה. אֶת הַגְּלוּיִים לָֽנוּ וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינָם גְּלוּיִים לָֽנוּ. אֶת הַגְּלוּיִים לָֽנוּ כְּבָר אֲמַרְנוּם לְפָנֶֽיךָ. וְהוֹדִֽינוּ לְךָ עֲלֵיהֶם. וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינָם גְּלוּיִם לָֽנוּ לְפָנֶֽיךָ הֵם גְּלוּיִים וִידוּעִים. כַּדָּבָר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ. וְהַנִּגְלֹת לָֽנוּ וּלְבָנֵֽינוּ עַד עוֹלָם. לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת: כִּי אַתָּה סָלְחָן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּמָחֳלָן לְשִׁבְטֵי יְשֻׁרוּן בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר וּמִבַּלְעָדֶֽיךָ אֵין לָֽנוּ מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹחֵל וְסוֹלֵֽחַ אֶלָּא אָֽתָּה:


For [transgressing] positive commandments, and for [transgressing] prohibitive commandments, whether the prohibition can be corrected by a specifically prescribed act,⁸⁴ or whether it cannot be corrected by a specifically prescribed act, for those of which we are aware and for those of which we are not aware. For those of which we are aware, we have already declared before You and confessed them unto You; and for those of which we are not aware, before You they are revealed and known, as it is said, “The hidden things belong to Adonoy, our God, but the revealed things are for us and for our children forever, that we might fulfill all the words of this Torah.”⁸⁵ For You are the Pardoner of Yisrael, and the Forgiver of the tribes of Yeshurun in every generation, and beside You, we have no King Who forgives and pardons—only You!

footnotes:
⁸⁴ For example returning the stolen money would be a corrective measure for the prohibition of stealing.
⁸⁵ Devorim 29:28.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 105

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/105](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/105)


אֱלֹהַי. עַד שֶׁלֹּא נוֹצַֽרְתִּי אֵינִי כְדַאי, וְעַכְשָׁו שֶׁנּוֹצַֽרְתִּי כְּאִלּוּ לֹא נוֹצַֽרְתִּי. עָפָר אֲנִי בְּחַיָּי. קַל וָחֹֽמֶר בְּמִיתָתִי. הֲרֵי אֲנִי לְפָנֶֽיךָ כִּכְלִי מָלֵא בוּשָׁה וּכְלִמָּה. יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי שֶׁלֹּא אֶחֱטָא עוֹד. וּמַה שֶּׁחָטָֽאתִי לְפָנֶֽיךָ מָרֵק בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים. אֲבָל לֹא עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִים וָחֳלָיִם רָעִים:


God, before I was formed, I was unworthy [to be created]. And now that I have been formed, it is as if I had not been formed. I am like dust while I live, how much more so when I am dead. Here I am before You like a vessel filled with shame. May it be Your will, Adonoy, my God, and the God of my fathers, that I shall sin no more, and the sins I have committed before You, cleanse them in Your abundant mercies; but not through suffering and severe illness.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 106

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/106](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/106)


אֱלֹהַי נְצוֹר לְשׁוֹנִי מֵרָע וּשְׂפָתַי מִדַּבֵּר מִרְמָה וְלִמְקַלְלַי נַפְשִׁי תִדּוֹם וְנַפְשִׁי כֶּעָפָר לַכֹּל תִּהְיֶה פְּתַח לִבִּי בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ וּבְמִצְוֹתֶֽיךָ תִּרְדּוֹף נַפְשִׁי וְכֹל הַחוֹשְׁבִים עָלַי רָעָה מְהֵרָה הָפֵר עֲצָתָם וְקַלְקֵל מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם: עֲשֵׂה לְמַֽעַן שְׁמֶֽךָ, עֲשֵׂה לְמַֽעַן יְמִינֶֽךָ, עֲשֵׂה לְמַֽעַן קְדֻשָּׁתֶֽךָ, עֲשֵׂה לְמַֽעַן תּוֹרָתֶֽךָ. לְמַֽעַן יֵחָלְצוּן יְדִידֶֽיךָ הוֹשִֽׁיעָה יְמִינְךָ וַעֲנֵֽנִי: יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה צוּרִי וְגוֹאֲלִי:


My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceitfully. To those who curse me, may my soul be unresponsive; and let my soul be like dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah and let my soul pursue Your commandments. And all who plan evil against me, quickly annul their counsel and frustrate their intention. Act for the sake of Your Name. Act for the sake of Your right hand. Act for the sake of Your holiness. Act for the sake of Your Torah. In order that Your loved ones be released, deliver [with] Your right hand and answer me. May the words of my mouth be acceptable and the thoughts of my heart — before You Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.

עֹשֶׂה הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן:


He Who makes the peace in His high heavens may He make peace upon us and upon all Yisrael and say Amein.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Amidah 108

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/108](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Amidah/r/108)


יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵֽינוּ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵֽנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ: וְשָׁם נַעֲבָדְךָ בְּיִרְאָה כִּימֵי עוֹלָם וּכְשָׁנִים קַדְמוֹנִיּוֹת: וְעָרְבָה לַיהֹוָה מִנְחַת יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלָֽםִ כִּימֵי עוֹלָם וּכְשָׁנִים קַדְמוֹנִיּוֹת:


May it be Your will, Adonoy, our God, and the God of our Fathers that the Holy Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days, and grant us our share in Your Torah. And there we will serve You reverently as in the days of old, and in earlier years. And let Adonoy be pleased with the offerings of Yehudah and Yerushalayim as in the days of old and in earlier years.

**בָּרוּךְ**אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים וְקוֹנֵה הַכֹּל וְזוֹכֵר חַסְדֵי אָבוֹת וּמֵבִיא גוֹאֵל לִבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶם לְמַֽעַן שְׁמוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה:


**Blessed** are You, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, God of Avraham, God of Yitzchak, and God of Yaakov, the Almighty, the Great, the Powerful, the Awesome, most high Almighty, Who bestows beneficent kindness, Who possesses everything, Who remembers the piety of the Patriarchs, and Who brings a redeemer to their children's children, for the sake of His Name, with love.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Reader's Repetition of the Amidah 5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Reader%27s%20Repetition%20of%20the%20Amidah/r/5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Reader%27s%20Repetition%20of%20the%20Amidah/r/5)


מִסּוֹד חֲכָמִים וּנְבוֹנִים. וּמִלֶּֽמֶד דַּֽעַת מְבִינִים. אֶפְתְּחָה פִי בִּתְפִלָּה וּבְתַחֲנוּנִים. לְחַלּוֹת וּלְחַנֵּן פְּנֵי מֶֽלֶךְ מוֹחֵל וְסוֹלֵֽחַ לַעֲו‍ֹנִים:


Invoking the doctrines of our wise and understanding Sages,¹ and with the teachings [acquired] from their perceptive intuition, I open my mouth in prayer and supplication to plead and seek favor before the presence of the King, Forgiver and Pardoner of iniquities.

footnotes:
¹ The Chazzan requests permission to interrupt the blessings of Shemoneh Esreh with the insertion of the piyyutim, declaring that the custom to do so is based on the teaching of our Sages.


###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Reader's Repetition of the Amidah 6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Reader%27s%20Repetition%20of%20the%20Amidah/r/6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Reader%27s%20Repetition%20of%20the%20Amidah/r/6)


**אֵימֶֽךָ**נָשָֽׂאתִי חִין בְּעָרְכִי. בְּמַלְאֲכוּת עַמְּךָ בֶּֽרֶךְ בְּבָרְכִי: גּוֹחִי מִבֶּֽטֶן הַגִּיהַּ חָשְׁכִּי. דַּבֵּר צָחוֹת וּבַאֲמִתְּךָ הַדְרִיכִי: הוֹרֵֽנִי שְׁפֹךְ שִֽׂיחַ עָרֵב. וְלוֹנְנִי בְצִלְּךָ אוֹתִי לְקָרֵב: זַֽעַק יוּפַק בְּכִוּוּן קֶֽרֶב. חַלּוֹתִי פָנֶֽיךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ תְקָרֵב: טְהוֹר עֵינַיִם מְאֹד נַעֲלָה. יַדְּעֵֽנִי בִין עֵֽרֶךְ תְּפִלָּה: כַּדָּת לְחַנֵּן בְּלִי תִפְלָה. לְהַמְצִיא לְשׁוֹלְחַי אֶֽרֶךְ וּתְעָלָה: מִפְתַּח שְׂפָתַי תְּבָרֵר וּתְיַשֵּׁר. נִדְבוֹת פִּי רְצֵה וְהַכְשֵׁר: סֵדֶר הֲגִיגִי כְּשַׁי יִתָּשֵׁר. עֶֽתֶר פִּצְחִי כְּזִלַּת חֶֽשֶׁר: פְּעָמַי הָכֵן פְּצוֹתִי מִכֶּֽשֶׁל. צוּר תְּמֹךְ אֲשׁוּרַי מֵהִנָּשֵׁל: קוֹמְמֵֽנִי וְחַזְּקֵֽנִי מֵרִפְיוֹן וָחֵֽשֶׁל. רְצוֹת אֲמָרַי וְלֹא אֶכָּשֵׁל: שָׁמְרֵֽנִי כְּאִישׁוֹן מִפֶּֽלֶץ וּבְעָתָה. שׁוּר בְּשִׁפְלוּתִי וּלְכָה לִישׁוּעָֽתָה: תָּחוֹן דִּכְאוּתִי כִּלְחוֹזָךְ פַּֽצְתָּ. תְּרַחֵם עַל בֵּן אִמַּֽצְתָּ:


I bear Your awe as I set forth my plea, in the service of Your people, I bend my knees. You [Who] took me out of the womb, brighten my darkness; let me speak clearly, and lead me in Your truth. Teach me to pour forth sweet meditation, and shelter me in Your shadow; bring me near to You. My cry comes forth with deep concentration; I seek Your Presence; and may Your righteousness be near. [God], Pure of sight and greatly exalted, grant me understanding to set forth my prayer, properly to entreat You—without fault, to find healing relief for those who sent me. The opening [words] of my lips, purify and set straight. [With] the offerings of my mouth, be pleased, and make them worthy; may the order of my prayer, be pleasing as a sacrifice, may my plea be [welcome] as raindrops. Direct my steps that my speech not falter, [my] Rock, support my steps from falling; uphold and strengthen me from weakness and exhaustion, be pleased with my words and let me not stumble. Preserve me as the apple of Your eye, [keep me] from trembling and terror; regard my low state and come [be my] deliverance. Be gracious to me for my spirit is broken, as You spoke to Your prophet, have compassion on the son You strengthened.

אִמַּֽצְתָּ עָשׂוֹר לְכִפּוּר תַּֽמָּה. בּוֹ לְצַחְצֵֽחַ צֵאוּי כִּתְמָהּ. גְּהֹץ צַחֲנָתָהּ עִוּוּיָהּ לְהָתֵֽמָּה. דִּינָהּ לְהָאִיר לְתֶֽחִי לְחָתֵֽמָה: הוּחֲרָֽדָה מִתֵּֽקַע יוֹם תְּרוּעָה. וּדְבָרִים קָֽחָה סַרְעַף לְקָרְעָה. זֶה אֵלִי לְצֶֽדֶק הַכְרִֽיעָה. חַי חַי יוֹדֽוּךָ בְּהָרִֽיעָה: טַפֶּֽיהָ וִישִׁישֶֽׁיהָ בְּעִנּוּי עֲיֵפִים. יְצִיגָתָם שׁוּר בְּיָחֵף יְחֵפִים. כֻּלָּם צָגִים וְלֹֽבֶן מֻצְעָפִים. לְאַדְּרָךְ בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ כִּשְׂרָפִים עָפִים: מָגֵן עִקָּרֵֽמוֹ בָּךְ חוֹסִים. נִשְׁעָנִים בְּתֻמָּם וּבְצִלְּךָ חוֹסִים. סְמוּכִים בִּבְרִית שְׁלֽשֶׁת יִחוּסִים. עוֹדְדֵם הֱיוֹת שׂוֹטְנֵֽימוֹ הָסִים: פְּנֵה בְּצִדְקַת אָת מֵעֵֽבֶר. צֹאנְךָ תַּֽחַת שֵֽׁבֶט כְּהַעֲבֵר. קַדְּמֵם רַחֲמֶֽיךָ בְּלִי הִתְעַבֵּר. רַחוּם עַל פֶּֽשַׁע עוֹבֵר: שֶֽׁמֶץ זְדוֹנָם תְּכַבֵּס וּתְטַהֵר. שַׁוְעָם קְשֹׁב וְאַל תְּאַחֵר: חזן תְּמוּכֵי יְמִינְךָ פְּנֵיהֶם נַהֵר. תִּעְתּֽוּעַ חֶטְאָם תְּכַפֵּר לְטַהֵר: כַּצָּהֳרַֽיִם מִשְׁפָּטֵֽנוּ הָאֵר. חוֹכֶֽיךָ לְטוֹב תַּשְׁאֵר: חזן צִדְקֵֽנוּ תְּחַפֵּשׂ וּתְבָאֵר. בְּמָגִנְּךָ נִתְגּוֹנֵן לְהִתְפָּאֵר:

זָכְרֵֽנוּ לְחַיִּים מֶֽלֶךְ חָפֵץ בַּחַיִּים וְכָתְבֵֽנוּ בְּסֵֽפֶר הַחַיִּים לְמַעַנְךָ אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים:

אַתָּה גִבּוֹר לְעוֹלָם אֲדֹנָי מְחַיֶּה מֵתִים אַתָּה רַב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ: מְכַלְכֵּל חַיִּים בְּחֶֽסֶד מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים בְּרַחֲמִים רַבִּים סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים וְרוֹפֵא חוֹלִים וּמַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים וּמְקַיֵּם אֱמוּנָתוֹ לִישֵׁנֵי עָפָר, מִי כָמֽוֹךָ בַּֽעַל גְּבוּרוֹת וּמִי דּֽוֹמֶה לָּךְ מֶֽלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה וּמַצְמִֽיחַ יְשׁוּעָה:


You are mighty forever, my Master; You are the Resurrector of the dead the Powerful One to deliver us. Sustainer of the living with kindliness, Resurrector of the dead with great mercy, Supporter of the fallen, and Healer of the sick, and Releaser of the imprisoned, and Fulfiller of His faithfulness to those who sleep in the dust. Who is like You, Master of mighty deeds, and who can be compared to You? King Who causes death and restores life, and causes deliverance to sprout forth.

תַּאֲוַת נֶֽפֶשׁ לְשִׁמְךָ וּלְזִכְרָךְ. שְׁקֹד לְרַחֵם מְבָרְכֵי זִכְרָךְ. רְצֽוּיֵי אַֽהַב כְּנַֽעַר וָרָךְ. קְרוּאִים וּנְקוּבִים בְּנָךְ בְּכוֹרָךְ: צִבְאוֹת קֹֽדֶשׁ הוֹצֵֽאתָ מִכּוּר אוֹנִים. פְּדוֹתָם מִפֶּֽרֶךְ הָלְכוּ שִׁנְאַנִּים. עֲמוּסִים מִבֶּֽטֶן פְּצֵם מִשְּׁאוֹנִים. סְעָדֵם בַּל לָמוֹד כִּסְאוֹנִים: נְתוּנָה בִּבְרִיתְךָ חֹק בִּשְׁאֵרָם. מִמַּחֲצֶֽבֶת צוּרָם מוֹלֶֽדֶת שְׁאוֹרָם. לַבְּרִית הַבֵּט וְתָדִֽיחַ כִּעוּרָם. כַּבְּסֵם הֶֽרֶב וְתַבְהִיק אוֹרָם: יֵרָאֶה לְפָנֶֽיךָ עֵֽקֶד מְיֻחָד. טוֹבֵֽחַ וְטָבוּחַ מִדְּבָרְךָ פָּחַד. חֲנִיטָיו חַלֵּץ מֵאֵימָֽתָה וָפַֽחַד. זִבּוּחוֹ וְדִשּׁוּנוֹ לְפָנֶֽיךָ יִתְיַֽחַד: וְאִם הֶעֱווּ אֹֽרַח לְסַלֵּף. הִזָּכֵר רַחֲמֶֽיךָ חֹק מִלְּחַלֵּף. דְּרִֽישַׁת צֶֽדֶק מֵלִיץ יְאַלֵּף. גְּנוּנֶֽיךָ לְחַזֵּק בְּמָגִנַּת אָֽלֶף: בַּדֵּי יְדִידֶֽיךָ הֲגִיגָם בִּין. בְּצוּרָם תִּֽישַׁע וְחֵטְא תַּלְבִּין: חזן אָֽוֶן מִתְחַנְּנֶֽיךָ בְּלִי תָבִין. אֶֽנֶק שְׁמַע וְלַֽחַשׁ הָבִין: נֶֽפֶשׁ נַעֲנָה תְּבַשֵּׂר סְלִיחָה. פַּלְּטֵם מֵעֹֽמֶק שׁוּחָה: חזן מִתְקוֹמְמֵֽינוּ יְהוּ כַסּוּחָה. הַחֲיֵֽינוּ בְטַל אֱמוּנָתְךָ לְשׂוֹחֵחָה:

###### Machzor Yom Kippur Ashkenaz, The Morning Prayers, Reader's Repetition of the Amidah 15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Reader%27s%20Repetition%20of%20the%20Amidah/r/15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Machzor%20Yom%20Kippur%20Ashkenaz/s/The%20Morning%20Prayers,_Reader%27s%20Repetition%20of%20the%20Amidah/r/15)


אֱנוֹשׁ מַה יִּזְכֶּה. וּצְבָא דוֹק לֹא זַכּוּ בְעֵינֶֽיךָ: בַּלַּחִים אִם תִּבְעַר הָאֵשׁ. מַה בֶּחָצִיר יָבֵשׁ: גָּלוּי לְךָ חֽשֶׁךְ כְּמוֹ אוֹר. מְשׁוֹטֵט כֹּל בְּעַֽיִן: דִּירָתְךָ בַּסֵֽתֶר. וּגְלוּיוֹת לְךָ כָּל נִסְתָּרוֹת: הַדָּן יְחִידִי. וְהוּא בְאֶחָד וּמִי יְשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ: וְעַל גּוֹי וְעַל אָדָם יַֽחַד יִנְטֶה קָו. וְאֵין מִי יַרְשִֽׁיעַ: זֹאת יָבִין כָּל יְצִיר. וְלֹא יַתְעוֹ יֶֽצֶר. לַחֲטוֹא לַיּוֹצֵר: חֲתֻלַּת בְּאֵרוֹ. חֲפִירַת בּוֹרוֹ. חֶשְׁבּוֹן בּוֹרְאוֹ: טָמֵא מִשְּׁאֵרוֹ. וּמִטַּמֵּא בְעוֹדוֹ. וּמְטַמֵּא בְמוֹתוֹ: יְמֵי חַיָּיו תֹּֽהוּ. וְלֵילוֹתָיו בֹּֽהוּ. וְעִנְיָנָיו הָֽבֶל: כַּחֲלוֹם מֵהָקִיץ נִדְמָה. בַּלָּהוֹת יְבַעֲתֽוּהוּ תָמִיד: לַֽיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁכַּב. יוֹמָם לֹא יָנֽוּחַ. עַד יֻרְדַּם בַּקָּֽבֶר: מַה יִּתְאוֹנֵן אָדָם חַי. דַּיּוֹ אֲשֶׁר הוּא חָי: נוֹלַד לְעָמָל וִיגִיעָה. אַשְׁרָיו אִם יְהִי יְגִיעוֹ בְּדַת אֱמֶת: סוֹפוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ מוֹכִֽיחַ. וְלָֽמָּה יַחֲנִיף: עוֹד חוֹתָמוֹ מְעִידוֹ עַל פָּעֳלוֹ. וּמַה יִּגְנֹב דַּֽעַת: פּוֹעֵל צְדָקוֹת אִם יְהִי. יְלַוּֽוּהוּ לְבֵית עוֹלָמוֹ: צוֹפֶה בְחָכְמָה אִם יְהִי. עִמּוֹ תִּתְלוֹנֵן בְּכֶלְחוֹ: קָצוּף בְּדָמִים וּבְמִרְמָה אִם יְהִי. חֲרוּצִים יָמָיו: רְצוֹנוֹ וְחֶפְצוֹ בִּהְיוֹת בְּמוּסָר. יָנוּב בְּשֵׂיבָה טוֹבָה: חזן שֵׁם טוֹב אִם יִקְנֶה. מִשֵּׁמוֹת נְעִימִים אֲשֶׁר יִקָּרֵא: תַּֽחַת כֵּן לָכֵן יוֹם הַמִּיתָה. מִיּוֹם לֵדָה הוּטַב:


¿Cómo puede el hombre ser meritorio ante Ti, pues aún Tus huestes angelicales no logran Tu beneplácito? Cuando los árboles lozanos son presa de llamas, ¿qué podrá hacer el heno fenecido? Tu omnisciencia todo devela, Tu luz ilumina todo lo tenebroso. Tu morada es objeto de misterio, mas Tú develas nuestros más ocultos designios. Sólo Tú eres juez Único, Tu voluntad es única, ¿quién osaría contrariarla? Tú sometes a pueblos e individuos a Tu justicia, ¿quién podría impugnar Tu justicia? Tenga presente todo ser esta enseñanza, para que su corazón no se desvíe en pos de sus instintos para que no erre ante su Creador: ¿De dónde procede, cuál es su origen? ¿Hacia dónde va? ¡Ante Dios su creador tendrá que rendir cuentas! ¿Cuál es el sentido de su vida? Sus días carecen de sentido, sus noches no tienen significado. ¡Todos sus proyectos vanidad! Cual sueño fugaz es su vida, cual pesadilla que con constancia lo atormenta. De noche no encuentra quietud, de día no reposa, y así transcurre su vida hasta que desciende al sepulcro. Mas ¿por qué habrá de quejarse el hombre mientras vive? La vida debería bastarle. Pues aunque su tarea es ardua, e ímproba su labor, feliz el hombre que se entrega a la ley y a la verdad. Su mismo fin testifica su origen ¿por qué habrá de vivir en ficción? Él mismo rubrica sus actos, ¿cómo podrá disimularlos? Únicamente sus buenas acciones lo conducirán hasta su eterna morada. Si la sabiduría él ha buscado, ella lo acompañará hasta el fin de sus días. Mas si el engaño y la perfidia él ha sembrado, su vida él ha condenado. Mas una vida de virtud, proporciona una vejez lozana y próspera.

מִי כָמֽוֹךָ אַב הָרַחֲמִים זוֹכֵר יְצוּרָיו לְחַיִּים בְּרַחֲמִים:

וְנֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לְהַחֲיוֹת מֵתִים: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים:

אִחַֽדְתָּ יוֹם זֶה בַּשָּׁנָה. תְּרוּפָה וְצָרִי שַׂמְתּוֹ לְשׁוֹשַׁנָּה. בְּשָׁלֵם בִּהְיוֹת סֻכָּךְ בָּרִאשֹׁנָה. שֵׁרוּתוֹ כִּפֵּר פִּשְׁעֵי יְשֵׁנָה: גּוֹלִים מִנָּוָךְ זְרוּיִים מֵהָֽלְאָה. רוֹן מְפִיקִים לְחַתֵּל תְּלָאָה. דִּכְּאוּת רֽוּחַ וָשֶֽׁבֶר נַהֲלָאָה. קָדוֹשׁ חֲשׁוֹב כְּזִבְחֵי הַעֲלָאָה: הֻתְמָם מֵרֶֽחֶם יוֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים. צוּרָתוֹ בְּכִסְאֲךָ חַֽקְתָּ כְּהִלִּים. וְלָדָיו חוֹן בְּעֹֽצֶר נִקְהָלִים. פְּאֵרְךָ מַבִּיעִים וְשִׁמְךָ מְהַלְּלִים: זֶֽבֶד שִׁמְךָ שִׁתַּֽפְתָּ בִּשְׁמָם. עֲמוּתִים לְךָ כַּחוֹתָם לְשׂוּמָם. חָשְׂכֵם מֵאֶֽנֶף בְּלִי לְהַאֲשִׁימָם. סֵֽפֶר חַיִּים יְהִי רִשּׁוּמָם: טֹֽרַח עָו‍ֹן וְכֹֽבֶד מַשָּׂא. נַעֵר בְּצוּל מְחוֹת בַּהֲמָסָה. יֶעֱרַב שִֽׂיחַ עֲנִיָּה וּרְמוּסָה. מִנִּיחוֹחֵי כָלִיל בְּאֶֽבֶן מַעֲמָסָה: כְּלוּלַת אֲהָבִים אָנָּא זְכֹר. כְּלִמַּת נְעוּרִים עוֹד מִלִּזְכֹּר: חזן לְבֶן יַקִּירָךְ זָכֹר תִּזְכֹּר. לְמַֽעַן חִלָּךְ לַעֲבָדֶֽיךָ זְכֹר:


*Oficiante:*
Bienaventurado el hombre que se hizo de buen nombre, pues es ese el mejor de los títulos. Si así lo hiciere entonces para él será: “mejor el día de la muerte que el día del nacimiento”.

**אַתָּה** הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ: בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ: גִּבּוֹר וְנַעֲרָץ: דָּגוּל מֵרְבָבָה: הוּא שָׂח וַיֶּהִי: וְצִוָּה וְנִבְרָאוּ: זִכְרוֹ לָנֶצַח: חַי עוֹלָמִים: טְהוֹר עֵינַיִם: יוֹשֵׁב סֵתֶר: כִּתְרוֹ יְשׁוּעָה: לְבוּשׁוֹ צְדָקָה: מַעֲטֵהוּ קִנְאָה: נֶאְפָּד נְקָמָה: סִתְרוֹ יוֹשֶׁר: עֲצָתוֹ אֱמוּנָה: פְּעֻלָּתוֹ אֱמֶת: צַדִּיק וְיָשָׁר: קָרוֹב לְקוֹרְאָיו בֶּאֱמֶת: רָם וּמִתְנַשֵּׂא: שׁוֹכֵן שְׁחָקִים: תּוֹלֶה אֶרֶץ עַל בְּלִימָה:


**You** are our God, in heaven and upon earth, mighty and revered! Surrounded with myriad angels, He spoke and it [the world] was! He commanded and all was created! His mention [Name] is eternal! Life of [all] the worlds, He is of pure eyes!² He dwells in concealment, His crown is deliverance!³ His garment is righteousness, His robe is zeal! He is clothed with vengeance His secret is uprightness!⁴ His counsel is faithful, His work is truth! He is just and upright, He is near to those who call upon Him in truth! Exalted and uplifted, He dwells in the heavens! He suspends the earth in space!

footnotes:
² Chavakuk 1:13.
³ Yeshaya 59:17.
⁴ The uprightness of the Almighty is not always revealed to us.

אַךְ אָתִים בְּחִין לְפָנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ בּוֹטְחִים בְּחַסְדְּךָ אֱמוּנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ גּוֹעִים וּמַרְגִּישִׁים שִׁכְנֶֽךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ דַּֽלּוּ עֵינֵיהֶם לִמְעוֹנֶֽךָ. חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ הוֹגִים לַעֲנוֹת עִנְיָנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ וְעוּדִים בְּנִצּֽוּחַ לְנַגְּנֶֽךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ זוֹעֲקִים יַֽחַד הֲמוֹנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ חוֹכִים יְשׁוּעוֹת חוֹסְנֶֽיךָ. חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ טְבוּלִים בְּטֹֽהַר לְחַנְּנֶֽךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ יוֹדוּ לְשִׁמְךָ בָּנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ מַאֲמִינֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ לֹא לָֽנוּ כִּי אִם לְמַעֲנֶֽךָ. חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ מַגֵּר מִתְקוֹמְמֵי צְפוּנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ נַשְּׂאֵם זֶֽרַע בְּחוּנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ סְלִיחָה תַּרְבֶּה לְמִתְעַנֶּֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ עֲנֵם מִשְּׁמֵי מְעוֹנֶֽךָ. חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ פְּצֵם מֵהֶמְיַת שְׁאוֹנֶֽךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ צַדֵּק גּוֹי נְבוֹנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ קוֹמֵם קֶֽדֶם קִנְיָנֶֽךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ רוֹמֵם תֵּל אַרְמוֹנֶֽךָ. חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ שְׁעֵה לַֽחַשׁ מִתְחַנְּנֶֽיךָ. כִּי אַתָּה רַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ תָּמְכֵם וְחָשְׂכֵם מֵחֲרוֹנֶֽךָ. חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל: אַךְ חַנּוּן אַתָּה וְרַחוּם לְכָל פֹּֽעַל:
